BIOS looked for boot code in the first 440 bytes of a disk. Not a file. A fixed offset. I used that model for years without thinking about it.

UEFI reads a FAT32 partition instead and keeps a list of boot entries in NVRAM. That is the reason two operating systems can sit on one disk without one install clobbering the other's bootloader.

The 2 TB limit everyone hit around 2010 was MBR arithmetic, not a disk problem.
